info.title: Mockingbird
info.description:
Stable, deterministic mock APIs for n8n courses, demos, and content.

## Authentication

- **Tier 1** (Product Catalogue, Weather, Exchange Rates, Quotes, Utilities, Fun Pack): no auth. IP rate-limited only.
- **Tiers 2-4**: every request needs `X-Api-Key` (see the schemes below) **and** an id header. A key alone isn't enough. Get a key from the dashboard (`/login`) or `just issue-key <course-slug>`. The id header is either `X-Assessment-Id` (the opaque id an Academy course issued you) or `X-Sandbox-Id` (not on a course? mint your own with `GET /v1/sandbox-id`, ADR-0020). Either is any 8-64 char id (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) namespacing your own sandbox writes from everyone else's; send just one of the two.
- **Auth Playground** (T2-AUTH) and **OAuth2 Provider** (Tier 3) use their own schemes per sub-path instead, see each endpoint's description.

A missing/invalid `X-Api-Key` is `401`; a missing/malformed id header is `422` `application/problem+json` naming both header options.

post.summary: Create or update an assessment from a YAML config
post.description:
Body: the assessment's YAML config, raw: the whole `.yaml` file's contents as the
request body (no JSON wrapper, no multipart upload). Validates it exactly like the
bundled example configs are validated, then upserts by `slug`: an existing slug is
replaced and reactivated. Refreshes the in-memory registry immediately, no separate
reload call needed. `course` in the config must already exist.

Configs created this way must embed their submission JSON Schema inline
(`submission.schema_inline`), since there is no filesystem to reference a file from.

delete.description:
Soft-delete: sets `active=false` and refreshes the in-memory registry (so it
disappears from `GET /v1/assessments` immediately). The row itself stays in the
database: `POST /internal/assessments` with the same slug reactivates it.
